correctness.rationale: PASS: Classical weighted multipartite spanning-tree generating identity specializes at root v to P_v(z)=z((N-1+z)/N)^(r-2) product_{j!=i}((N-n_j-1+z)/(N-n_j))^(n_j-1). Because other part sizes are >=1, the root at -(N-1) occurs precisely r-2 times; roots at -(N-t-1) give (t-1) per nonroot part of size t>=2, after removing compulsory z at t=N-1. The remaining r-1 other parts are singletons, and known N gives root-part size. This works for r=2, complete graphs, stars, N=2. Independent exact weighted Kirchhoff cofactors on five multipartite types and all root part types at z=1,2,5 matched the stated normalized PGF; full proof is algebraic and not an extrapolation from finite tests.

evidence: Earlier co-degree result recovers parts only from all pair co-degrees and assumes n_i>=2; no single rooted tree-degree probability is involved.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General forward spanning-tree distributions apply to many graphs but do not imply the inverse uniqueness across host graphs; co-degree graph reconstruction is a different invariant (all pair common neighbor values) and a smaller no-singleton graph family.

evidence: Nonroot size-t parts contribute exactly (t-1) multiplicity at -(N-t-1); multiplicities and N force the entire multiset, even singleton parts.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The old multivariate enumerator gives expression (2) but a theorem about distribution uniqueness requires comparing potential different host-size profiles and proving the inverse decoder, including the hidden root part. Neither prior general UST degree moment formulas nor unrelated co-degree inverse establishes this assertion. It is a short but genuine structural consequence with a motivated natural inverse formulation.

evidence: Proof decodes r from root at 1-N, all nonroot non-singleton part sizes from negative roots and denominators (t-1), then singleton count and root part from N.

originality.rationale: PASS best of knowledge: Remmel–Williamson weighted spanning-tree enumerator is explicitly prior and gives forward joint generating functions; Rapoport general UST degree formulas and Fita Sanmartin et al node-degree moments are also forward. They do not state that one arbitrarily chosen vertex marginal, with its root part concealed, identifies every complete multipartite graph of known order. Prior co-degree reconstruction uses all common-neighbor pairs rather than one random rooted degree and excludes singleton parts. Exact inversion by factor multiplicities is a new natural injectivity assertion under tested sources.
residual_risks: Classical forward enumerator makes inverse factorization short; an unlocated earlier statement may explicitly characterize injectivity.
Exact probability law and known N are essential; numerical samples are not covered.
Original Remmel–Williamson publisher article was not read in full.

value.rationale: PASS: A natural one-vertex stochastic inverse graph problem admits a full all-order reconstruction, including highly asymmetric and singleton-containing complete multipartite graphs. This identifies a whole host isomorphism class from an exact scalar marginal and shows why N must be specified (universal star-leaf degree 1). The constructive root multiplicity decoder, though based on known enumerator, is a useful explicit local-to-global rigidity theorem.

limitations: Does not reconstruct general graphs or prove statistical identifiability from finite samples. Earlier classical enumerator credited fully.
